submissions.findingTextShort: A positive stable-angina trial administered Terminalia arjuna bark extract, not isolated arjunolic acid.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 58 men with chronic stable angina reported improved clinical and treadmill outcomes with Terminalia arjuna bark extract, but the administered extract contained multiple acids, glycosides, flavones, tannins, proanthocyanidins, minerals, and other constituents; the result cannot establish isolated arjunolic-acid efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Fifty-eight men with chronic stable angina and provocable ischemia
submissions.usageContext: Terminalia arjuna bark extract 500 mg every eight hours in a crossover trial
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Parent-botanical clinical evidence may contextualize constituent relevance but cannot donate treatment efficacy or dose to isolated arjunolic acid.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 100-patient heart-failure RCT studied Terminalia arjuna water extract, not isolated arjunolic acid.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled add-on trial in 100 patients with chronic heart failure administered standardized Terminalia arjuna stem-bark water extract rather than isolated arjunolic acid; the primary endpoint was change in left-ventricular ejection fraction, so any favorable or null outcomes remain whole-extract evidence and cannot be assigned to the constituent owner.
submissions.populationContext: One hundred patients with NYHA class II chronic heart failure on standard therapy
submissions.usageContext: Terminalia arjuna standardized stem-bark water extract 750 mg twice daily for 12 weeks
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Whole-botanical intervention identity prevents attribution to arjunolic acid; endpoint-level findings must remain attached to the parent extract.

submissions.findingTextShort: Direct isolated-arjunolic-acid human efficacy and dosing evidence remains unestablished by Terminalia trials.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The available clinical cardiovascular trials located for this evidence family administer Terminalia arjuna bark preparations containing many constituents, while the arjunolic-acid owner is a singular triterpenoid; direct isolated-compound human efficacy, dose, long-term safety, and interaction evidence therefore remain gaps and must not be backfilled from parent-botanical outcomes.
submissions.populationContext: Human Terminalia arjuna cardiovascular literature versus isolated arjunolic acid
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Research-gap conclusion; does not negate possible arjunolic-acid activity, but blocks unsupported clinical inheritance.

submissions.findingTextShort: Terminalia bark-extract regimens cannot become a consumer dose for isolated arjunolic acid.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human Terminalia arjuna trials use defined bark-extract regimens, such as 500 mg every eight hours in stable angina, but those product doses include many constituents and cannot be converted into an isolated arjunolic-acid dose; the current generic extract-style dosage on the compound owner therefore lacks proposition-compatible support.
submissions.populationContext: Patients receiving Terminalia arjuna bark extracts in clinical trials
submissions.usageContext: Dose-attribution boundary between whole extract and isolated constituent
submissions.uncertaintyNote: No isolated arjunolic-acid dosing recommendation is inferred.
